first.rationale: Two metrics (onboarding completion, activation) are down this quarter, and memory_31 and memory_86 both point to onboarding simplification as a reliable lever with durable activation gains, without flagged data-quality caveats. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pricing pressure, but that memory explicitly warns of a pooled-cohort redefinition mid-test, making its lift estimate unreliable; chasing price competition also risks training price-sensitive segments toward lower willingness-to-pay, undermining sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I want to verify memory_73's original record before ever acting on it, and verify memory_31 to confirm the onboarding lift is genuinely durable (not itself a pooled or short-window artifact) before committing our single experiment slot. Given only one experiment fits this week, I'm directing it at onboarding simplification as a small guarded test targeting the SMB segment most affected by the completion drop, rather than a broad rollout, since we haven't yet re-verified the underlying record and want to confirm effect size holds before scaling.
